prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an indoor corridor and retail/store area where a person in a dark shirt stays very bright in the foreground at roughly 0.5 to 1.2 metres in front of the camera wearer, while a handheld cell phone appears even brighter at the bottom center/right in frames 3 to 5 at about 0.3 to 0.4 metres (within the camera wearer's arm's reach). Across the 5 frames, the camera wearer turns and walks forward alongside and behind the other person, who shifts from center-right in frame 1 (facing right in profile, not looking at the camera wearer) to being partially cut off on the right edge in frames 2 and 3, before appearing directly ahead and to the left in frames 4 and 5 facing away; meanwhile, walls, windows, store shelves, and an accordion partition sit roughly 1.5 to 4 metres away to the left and right. In frames 4 and 5, both the camera wearer's phone and the adjacent shelves/doorway are within arm's reach of the foreground person and the camera wearer, with the person's torso and arm partially occluding the shelves in frame 4 and the dark doorway in frame 5. Compared to the heavily motion-blurred RGB frames, the depth map clearly separates the foreground person and the top edge of the close-up phone from the receding corridor wall and shelving planes. However, the map is unreliable around glass window panes in frame 1 and the open doorway in frame 5 (rendering them as flat black drop-offs), and it flattens the internal geometry of the person's back and the cluttered store shelves into smooth, featureless blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground person (pink mask) at roughly 0.5 to 1.2 metres ahead of the camera wearer across all 5 frames, as well as the camera wearer's cell phone (brown mask) at the bottom edge in frames 4 and 5 at about 0.3 to 0.4 metres, positioned below and slightly behind the person's right arm. As the camera wearer turns and follows the person from a windowed hallway into a store aisle and toward an exit doorway, the person's mask shifts from center in frame 1 (facing sideways to the right, looking away from the camera) to the far right edge in frames 2 and 3 (heavily cropped out of view), and back to center-left in frames 4 and 5 facing away with their right arm hanging within arm's reach of the camera wearer's phone and the doorway. In frames 4 and 5, the cell phone mask at the bottom slightly overlaps and occludes the lower edge of the person's hip and hand area, while the person's silhouette occludes the unsegmented shelving behind them. While the segmentation masks provide sharp silhouette boundaries for the person and cell phone despite severe motion blur in the RGB strip, they omit all orientation details and miss the cell phone tip already entering the bottom of frame 3. Furthermore, the map is highly unreliable for scene layout, failing to segment the retail shelves in frame 4 and misclassifying the windowed hallway wall in frame 3 as a 'train' (tan mask) and the folding door partition on the right of frame 5 as a 'refrigerator' (green mask) at about 1.5 metres distance.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 through 4 and detects only a single magenta right-hand skeleton in frame 5, corresponding to the foreground person's right hand hanging down to the right of their torso at roughly 0.6 to 0.8 metres in front of the camera wearer. Using the RGB context, this detected hand belongs to the person walking ahead and facing away from the camera wearer (never looking toward the camera), and it sits just above and slightly ahead of the camera wearer's handheld phone (about 0.2 to 0.3 metres apart) and within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the adjacent doorway. In frame 5, the pose map reveals the articulated finger keypoints and downward-cupped orientation of the person's right hand much more distinctly than the motion-blurred RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable for broader spatial understanding because it provides zero information about room layout, background objects, or distances across the first four frames. It completely fails to detect the person's yellow body skeleton in every frame—where the person's head and limbs are either blurred in frame 1 or partially cropped out of the frame boundaries in frames 2 through 5—and misses their right arm even when clearly visible in frame 4.
